newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-ELWAY SEES EARLY RETURN DESPITE ARM INJURY.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-ELWAY SEES EARLY RETURN DESPITE ARM INJURY.

text.p: Despite a torn right bicep tendon, Denver Broncos quarterback John Elway expects to return to action soon enough to play one more exhibition game.
Elway had a magnetic resonance imaging exam Tuesday to explore the extent of an injury to his throwing arm that he suffered in a preseason loss to the Miami Dolphins on Monday night in Mexico City.
Doctors say his recovery should take two to four weeks.
The Broncos visit Carolina on Saturday and New England on August 17 before a home game against San Francisco August 23 -- the game Elway apparently is aiming for.
"I'm planning on playing in one more preseason game," he said. "Now it's just a matter of getting the soreness out and going from there."

Broncos coach Mike Shanahan suggested Elway might be back even a week earlier than the 49ers game and said at a news conference that the injury was a "best-case scenario" because the tear was at the end of the tendon, near the shoulder.
He added that Elway could be throwing again by the end of the week.
"He's a tough son-of-a-gun," Shanahan said. "I wouldn't be surprised if he is back a little bit quicker."
Elway injured his right bicep while throwing a pass in the first quarter and did not return. He completed 5-of-8 passes for 62 yards.
"He wanted to go back in the game and we kept him out," Shanahan said. "Thank God we did because I think if he would have went back in he would have tore it completely."

The 37-year-old Elway was voted to his fifth Pro Bowl last season, throwing for 3,328 yards and 26 touchdowns. He has passed for 3,000 yards in 11 of his 14 NFL seasons and last year became the quarterback with the most wins in league history with 126.
Bubby Brister and Jeff Lewis are the backup quarterbacks for the Broncos. Each played Monday night.

Defensive end Alfred Williams also underwent an MRI Tuesday. It revealed a torn left triceps muscle that will sideline him for six weeks. Williams started all 16 regular-season games at right defensive tackle last season and was named to his first Pro Bowl.

Defensive end Neil Smith, signed as a free agent away from the rival Kansas City Chiefs, also left Monday's game with a bruised right knee. The recurring injury was not considered serious but Smith did not return to the game.
